subject: Human Evolution
title: Energy Efficiency
description: A quick win: understand Energy Efficiency.

hook.text: Walking on two legs uses 75% less energy than a chimp uses walking on four. That's a huge saving.

buildup.text: Bipedal walking turns the body into a pendulum—each step recovers energy from the one before.

discovery.text: When food is scarce and you must travel far, energy-efficient movement is a survival advantage.

twist.text: Chimps are actually efficient climbers. On the ground, though, bipedalism wins over their waddle.

climax.text: Natural selection didn't care about speed. It favored the locomotion that used fewer calories per km.

punchline.text: We didn't evolve to run fast. We evolved cheap.

quiz.question: Why is bipedal walking energy-efficient?
options: Two legs weigh less than four
